newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end lower as Wall Street falls.
newsitem.headline: German shares end lower as Wall Street falls.

text.p: German shares ended the day sharply lower on Friday, as a jittery market reacted harshly to a lower opening on Wall Street. Support for the IBIS DAX index of 30 blue chips held at 3,300 points held, however.
The IBIS DAX ended at 3,319.24 points, way off an intraday high of 3,381.18 points, having yo-yoed higher and lower over the day.
Earlier the DAX index, which tracks floor trade, ended the session at 3,340.05 points, down 11.44 points or 0.34 percent.

"People are very nervous and looking at every single figure. You could see that when the market fell like a stone after Wall Street opened. I remain positive in the medium term for the market," said a German equity analyst.
The car sector remained the main feature of the market.
"Porsche and Daimler were lifted by the overall good sentiment in the car sector. Daimler also has its annual news conference and an analysts' meeting on Wednesday next week," the analyst said.
He said that much of Friday's 12 percent rise in Volkswagen shares was down to a rash of analysts' upgrades early on.

"Also, the analysts' meeting only ended late in the day on Thursday and there was a bit of late demand coming. The share is down now and I think we will have a bit of a breather," said the analyst, who said he thought the share price could hit 1,500 marks this year.
Volkswagen AG was way off earlier highs by the end of trade, up eight marks at 1,054 marks, while BMW AG ended down was down 43.90 marks at 1,390.10 marks.
Daimler remained among the top gainers and ended up 3.95 marks, or three percent, at 135.50 marks. Porsche was up 87 marks, 4.5 percent, at 1,022 marks.
